A variable or process that can generate an observed association without the intended causal interpretation.
A feature of an experiment that influences participants through expectations about the study rather than the target mechanism.
Public or time-stamped specification of hypotheses, methods, analyses, and revision criteria before observing target results.
A prospective condition under which a claim should be rejected or substantially weakened.
An empirical or logical result that requires changing a term, dependency, model, or claim status.
A prediction on which competing theories or models expect observably different outcomes.
Prediction evaluated on data not used to fit or select the model.
Repeated partitioning or resampling used to estimate generalization while controlling model selection.
Independent repetition of a study or analysis to test robustness of a result.
Ability to obtain the same computational result from the same specified inputs, code, environment, and parameters.
Reproduction of a result from equations/specification without reusing the original implementation.
A comparison model or procedure against which improvement is assessed.
A baseline controlled to use comparable information, resources, and training restrictions.
Evaluation of competing models using declared predictive, explanatory, or complexity criteria.
Model comparison that accounts for complexity or flexibility so better fit cannot be purchased without cost.
A quantitative estimate of the magnitude of an observed effect.
An interval expressing uncertainty around an estimated quantity under a declared statistical method.
A model assigning inputs to categories; successful decoding does not prove system-effective information.
A mapping that extracts represented variables from system activity or state; decodability does not by itself establish causal use.
Comparison of relational structure among representations using pairwise similarity or distance matrices.
Ability of a model or metric learned on some participants to predict structured outcomes for other participants.
Stability of a model or metric across repeated measurement sessions.
Ability of a proposed variable or geometry to predict across different experimental paradigms.
Experimental design or analysis that distinguishes competing theories rather than merely finding a shared correlate.
A neural state or process reliably associated with consciousness under a declared contrast; correlation alone is not a constitutive explanation.
A mapping from an abstract organizational term to neural variables or mechanisms under explicit bridge assumptions.
Directed influence among neural or system variables estimated under a declared causal/dynamical model.
Statistical dependence among measured signals without necessarily establishing causal direction.
Activity localized to a region or component; magnitude alone need not capture distributed organization.
Coordinated dynamics among distributed neural or computational components.
Processing in which activity returns through feedback connections rather than remaining strictly feedforward.
A theoretical architecture in which selected information becomes broadly available across specialized processes.
Dynamics near a transition between regimes, often associated with sensitivity and broad timescales; criticality is not identified with consciousness by itself.
Transient persistence of coordinated neural configurations before transition to other configurations.
A multivariate description of neural and physiological variables over a declared time scale.
A biologically regulated state with characteristic behavioral and physiological patterns; phenomenality varies across sleep stages.
Conscious-like or phenomenal experience occurring during sleep in some states; report after waking is an indirect measure.
A state induced by anaesthetic agents with changes in responsiveness and conscious capacity that vary by drug, dose, and individual.
A clinical category involving impaired wakefulness and/or awareness; diagnosis requires validated clinical assessment.
Evidence of command-following brain activity in some behaviorally unresponsive patients; it complicates inference from overt behavior alone.
An altered state associated with psychedelic substances and changes in perception, self-experience, affect, and network dynamics; mechanisms depend on substance and context.
A state associated with meditation practice whose phenomenology and neural correlates vary by technique, expertise, and context.
A machine-readable record containing a stable term ID, definition, class, epistemic status, dependencies, source anchors, and computational bindings.
A typed directed or undirected relation between canonical term IDs.
A relation declaring that one term definition or computation depends on another canonical term.
A relation declaring explicit non-equivalence or forbidden semantic collapse between terms.
